Create new *_map() functions

Source: R/function-map.R
function_map.Rd

function_map() creates a basic mapper: a function that applies a single-case test such as grim_scalar() to every row of a data frame. grim_map(), grimmer_map(), and debit_map() are made by it.

See vignette("consistency-tests-in-depth"), section Creating basic mappers with function_map().

function_map() is a developer tool: it may change in a minor release, with a NEWS entry.

Usage

function_map(
  .fn,
  .reported = NULL,
  .name_test,
  .name_key_result = "consistency",
  .name_class = NULL,
  .args_disabled = NULL,
  .args_by_row = NULL,
  .args_fixed = NULL,
  .cols_helper = NULL,
  .col_names = NULL,
  .cols_derived = NULL,
  .reported_variadic = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

.fn

Single-case function to apply to each row. It must return a single logical value or, if .col_names is specified, a list of values with the key result first.

.reported

String. Names of the arguments of .fn that take the reported values, such as c("x", "n"). These become the key columns. May be NULL if .reported_variadic is specified. Key and helper columns named n, items_averaged, or absolute are taken to be whole numbers, as are the decimal counts of .args_by_row: a value within floating-point noise of one, such as 100 * 0.29, is rounded to it before .fn sees it.

.name_test

String (length 1). Plain-text name of the test, such as "GRIM".

.name_key_result

(Experimental) String (length 1). Name of the key result column. Default is "consistency".

.name_class

String. Optionally, one or more classes to add to the output. Default is NULL; see Details for the class that is always added.

.args_disabled

Optionally, names of arguments of .fn that the factory-made function should not have. Specifying one of them is an error.

.args_by_row

Optionally, names of arguments of .fn that may vary by row, such as "digits_x". The factory-made function takes a single value or one per row of data for each. If one is left out, it is read from a column of data by that name, if there is one. They are returned as columns. One whose name starts with digits_ is a decimal count, returned as integer like digits_x.

.args_fixed

Optionally, a named list of values that are always passed to .fn, such as list(show_reason = TRUE). The factory-made function has no arguments for them; specifying one is an error.

.cols_helper

Optionally, names of arguments of .fn that may also be given as columns of data, such as "items_averaged". A helper column is returned after the key columns if it was given, as a column or as an argument. Giving both is an error if they disagree.

.col_names

Optionally, names of the columns that a list returned by .fn unpacks into, as with show_rec = TRUE. The first name must be .name_key_result. If data has no rows, the columns are those that .fn returns for a row of missing values, or, if it fails on one, only the key result column.

.cols_derived

Optionally, a named list of vectorized functions that compute further columns from the same input, such as list(exp_incon = grim_exp_incon). Each is called once, with the whole columns and only the arguments it has formals for, and must return one value per row; a .reported_variadic argument comes as a list of each row's values. The columns follow the key result column.

.reported_variadic

Optionally, a single string naming an argument of .fn that takes the values of one row as a vector. The factory-made function gets an argument by that name, without a default, that selects any number of columns with tidyselect syntax. See Details.

...

These dots must be empty.

Value

A function with these arguments:

  • data: a data frame with the key columns. Other columns are permitted.

  • The .args_by_row arguments, such as digits_x.

  • If .reported_variadic was given, an argument by that name.

  • One argument per .reported value, for naming a column of data that holds that value under another name.

  • ...: must be empty. Every argument after it must be named in full.

  • The other arguments of .fn, i.e., those not named in .reported, .reported_variadic, .args_disabled, or .args_fixed, with the same defaults.

Details

.reported_variadic is for a test whose number of key columns depends on the data, such as whether the values in any number of columns add up to the value in another one. .fn takes those values as a single vector, and the factory-made function selects the columns with tidyselect; see Examples. The selection must not be empty and must not include a column that already has a role in the test. The selected columns are returned as themselves. Such a mapper cannot be wrapped by function_map_seq() or function_map_total_n(), which derive their arguments from .reported.

The output has the class "scrutiny_{tolower(.name_test)}_map", with spaces as underscores, e.g., "scrutiny_grim_map", in addition to any .name_class. The arguments that applied to the whole call, such as rounding, are recorded on the output; see scrutiny_meta().

Value returned by the factory-made function

A tibble with the .reported_variadic columns, the .reported columns, the helper columns that were given, the .args_by_row columns, and the key result column (consistency by default), which is TRUE for consistent value sets, FALSE for inconsistent ones, and NA if the test can't decide. Any .cols_derived columns, any .col_names columns, and the other columns of data follow, in that order.

Examples

# A single-case function for SCHLIM, a mock test:
schlim_scalar <- function(y, n) {
  (y / 3) > n
}

# The mapper:
schlim_map <- function_map(
  .fn = schlim_scalar,
  .reported = c("y", "n"),
  .name_test = "SCHLIM"
)

df1 <- tibble::tibble(y = 16:25, n = 3:12)
schlim_map(df1)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 3
#>        y     n consistency
#>    <int> <int> <lgl>      
#>  1    16     3 TRUE       
#>  2    17     4 TRUE       
#>  3    18     5 TRUE       
#>  4    19     6 TRUE       
#>  5    20     7 FALSE      
#>  6    21     8 FALSE      
#>  7    22     9 FALSE      
#>  8    23    10 FALSE      
#>  9    24    11 FALSE      
#> 10    25    12 FALSE      

# A test over any number of columns: do the parts add up to the total?
# The single-case function takes the parts as one vector...
sum_check_scalar <- function(parts, total, tolerance = 0) {
  abs(sum(parts) - total) <= tolerance
}

# ...which `.reported_variadic` names:
sum_check_map <- function_map(
  .fn = sum_check_scalar,
  .reported = "total",
  .reported_variadic = "parts",
  .name_test = "SUMCHECK"
)

df2 <- tibble::tibble(
  item_1 = c(10, 20, 30),
  item_2 = c(5, 5, 5),
  item_3 = c(1, 2, 3),
  total  = c(16, 27, 40)
)

# The `parts` argument selects columns with tidyselect syntax:
sum_check_map(df2, parts = starts_with("item"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   item_1 item_2 item_3 total consistency
#>    <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>      
#> 1     10      5      1    16 TRUE       
#> 2     20      5      2    27 TRUE       
#> 3     30      5      3    40 FALSE
